tweet.text:
Humanities research needs more than one answer. It needs competing paths.

MISAKA is a multi-agent research system for humanities and social sciences that turns a question into an auditable research process.

It helps you explore alternatives without losing the evidence trail by having a coordinator plan the inquiry, specialist agents research branches, and a red team review the conclusion before a final report is written.

Key features:

• Research graph – explores different ways a question could be answered, level by level
• Specialist teams – assigns research work to configurable specialists with their own skills and models
• Review loops – uses red-team and divergence reviews to surface gaps, alternatives, and untested premises
• Traceable citations – records citations to page and character offset, with source files kept alongside the research
• Local project outputs – stores plans, task cards, conclusions, critiques, and source lists as Markdown in the project folder

It’s open-source (Apache License 2.0 license).

Link in the reply 👇
